title: In-device key derivation: HKDF and PBKDF2 via the chardev
description:
No key derivation functions (KDF) are available via /dev/crypto2dev. Applications needing derived keys must:
1. Export master key material to userspace
2. Run KDF in userspace (OpenSSL, libsodium, etc.)
3. Import derived key back into kernel via KEY_IMPORT

This forces sensitive master key material through userspace and prevents FIPS-compliant key derivation within the FIPS boundary. SP 800-56C and SP 800-132 require KDFs to operate on keying material within the FIPS module boundary.

Minimum needed:
- HKDF (RFC 5869): extract-then-expand, HMAC-based. Used in TLS 1.3, SSH, Signal.
- PBKDF2 (RFC 8018 / SP 800-132): password-based. Used in PKCS#12, disk encryption.
- SP 800-108 counter-mode KBKDF: required by some USG/FIPS use cases.

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED:

(a) Which KDFs to support in v1?
  Option A: HKDF only (RFC 5869). Most broadly applicable; TLS 1.3 requires it.
  Option B: HKDF + PBKDF2. Adds password-based derivation for key storage use cases.
  Option C: All three (HKDF + PBKDF2 + KBKDF SP 800-108). Full FIPS coverage but significant scope.

(b) UAPI design — how should KDF operations be exposed?
  Option A: New OPERATION fd op type (e.g., CRYPTO2DEV_OP_KDF). INIT with algo='hkdf(sha256)', write() feeds IKM+salt+info, read() returns OKM. Fits existing fd model.
  Option B: One-shot ioctl CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_DO_KDF with all inputs inline in the struct. Consistent with DO_SIGN/DO_VERIFY/DO_AGREE pattern.
  Option C: KDF produces a KEY fd directly — output is not returned to userspace but immediately becomes a KEY fd usable for INIT. Keeps derived key material in kernel.

  Option C is the most secure (derived key never in userspace) and naturally extends the key fd model. But it requires the KDF output to be a known-size key (caller must specify target algo for the derived key fd).

(c) For PBKDF2: where does the password come from? Options:
  - write() feeds the password bytes (never returned)
  - Inline in the ioctl struct (up to CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_MAXLEN bytes)

Work items once decisions are made:
- Design UAPI structs/ioctls
- Implement in wolfssl provider (wc_HKDF, wc_PKCS5_PBKDF2 or equivalent)
- Implement in kcapi provider (kernel has HKDF via crypto_shash; PBKDF2 may need wolfCrypt)
- NIST test vectors exist for HKDF (RFC 5869 appendix A) and PBKDF2 (RFC 6070)
notes: BLOCKED: KDF design conflict — see bd human flag. out_algo field missing from impl vs design. Symmetric KEY fd support not in current system.
